revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Refueling the Lander
revealWordProblem.text: A space-station crew has 27.6 liters of fuel to load into the lander. Each fuel cell holds exactly 3.45 liters. How many fuel cells can the crew completely fill? Make the divisor a whole number first, then divide.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 27.6 ÷ 3.45 = 8 fuel cells. Multiply both numbers by 100 to make the divisor whole: 2760 ÷ 345 = 8. Check: 8 × 3.45 = 27.6 liters.

launch.narrative: This is your challenge small group for Lesson 2.7. You can already get the answer — so in here the answer is the starting point. We ask when the method holds, when it breaks, and how you would convince someone who disagrees.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do you divide with decimals?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Move the decimal point the same number of places in BOTH the divisor and the dividend, put the point in the quotient straight above it, then repeat Divide → Multiply → Subtract → Bring Down — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I want 18.9 ÷ 6.3. The divisor is 6.3, and long division needs a whole-number divisor.
STEP 0 — MOVE THE POINT: I move the decimal point 1 place right in the divisor, so 6.3 becomes 63.
I must move the dividend the same 1 place right: 18.9 becomes 189, and the point in the quotient goes straight above its new spot. The problem is now 189 ÷ 63.
DIVIDE: 63 does not fit into 1 or 18, so my first working number is 189. How many 63s fit into 189? Three. I write 3 above the 9.
BRING DOWN: there are no digits left to bring down, so the cycle is finished and the remainder is 0. 18.9 ÷ 6.3 = 3.
I check by multiplying: 6.3 × 3 = 18.9. Correct — 3 pods can be filled.

explore.instructions: Go deeper: Complete the table. First move the point so the divisor is a whole number, moving it the same number of places in both numbers. Then run the long-division cycle — divide, multiply, subtract, bring down — to find the quotient. As you work, ask yourself WHY it works.

discourse.prompt: Why does moving the point the same number of places in both numbers give you the same quotient — and why is it worth doing before you start the divide, multiply, subtract, bring down cycle?
discourse.sentenceFrame: Multiplying both numbers by ___ doesn't change the quotient because ___.

onLevel.stem: A water tank holds 19.2 liters. It is poured into bottles that each hold 1.6 liters. How many bottles can be filled?
choiceFeedback: Check the division: make the divisor a whole number by moving both decimals one place (192 ÷ 16), then divide.
That is one bottle more than the division gives. Multiply both numbers by 10 and divide 192 by 16 carefully — it comes out even, with nothing left over.
The digits look right—how many total decimal places should the product have?
hints: You're asking how many 1.6s fit into 19.2 — that's division, and the divisor 1.6 needs to become whole first.
Multiply both amounts by 10 to build an equivalent whole-number division, then divide.
19.2 × 10 = 192 and 1.6 × 10 = 16. Now run the cycle on 192 ÷ 16: DIVIDE 19 ÷ 16 → 1, MULTIPLY 1 × 16 = 16, SUBTRACT 19 − 16 = 3, BRING DOWN the 2.
onLevel.stemEs: Un tanque de agua contiene 19.2 litros. Se vacía en botellas que contienen 1.6 litros cada una. ¿Cuántas botellas se pueden llenar?
hintsEs: Estás preguntando cuántos 1.6 caben en 19.2: eso es división, y el divisor 1.6 debe volverse entero primero.
Multiplica ambas cantidades por 10 para armar una división equivalente de enteros y luego divide.
19.2 × 10 = 192 y 1.6 × 10 = 16. Ahora repite el ciclo en 192 ÷ 16: DIVIDE 19 ÷ 16 → 1, MULTIPLICA 1 × 16 = 16, RESTA 19 − 16 = 3, BAJA el 2.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Count how far to move
workedExample.work: 0.12 has 2 decimal places, so BOTH numbers move 2 places right. The divisor: 0.12 → 12.
workedExample.workEs: 0.12 tiene 2 lugares decimales, así que AMBOS números se mueven 2 lugares a la derecha. El divisor: 0.12 → 12.

workedExample.label: Move the dividend the same 2 places
workedExample.work: 9.6 only has one digit after the point, so the student moved it just 1 place: 9.6 → 96. New problem: 96 ÷ 12 = 8.
workedExample.labelEs: Mueve el dividendo los mismos 2 lugares
workedExample.workEs: 9.6 solo tiene un dígito después del punto, así que el estudiante lo movió solo 1 lugar: 9.6 → 96. Nuevo problema: 96 ÷ 12 = 8.

onLevel.correctWork: Both numbers must move the SAME number of places — 2, not 1. 9.6 runs out of digits after one place, so you add a placeholder zero to move the second place: 9.6 → 96 → 960. The real problem is 960 ÷ 12 = 80, so 9.6 ÷ 0.12 = 80. Estimate to confirm: 0.12 is tiny, so many of them fit in 9.6 — the quotient must be large, not 8. Check: 80 × 0.12 = 9.6. ✓
hints: The divisor moved 2 places (0.12 → 12), so the dividend has to move 2 places too — the student only moved it 1.
9.6 has no second digit to move, so add a placeholder zero: 9.6 → 960. Then 960 ÷ 12 = 80.
onLevel.explanation: In the last step the dividend moved only 1 place while the divisor moved 2, so the two numbers no longer match. Adding a placeholder zero lets 9.6 move both places to 960, making the real problem 960 ÷ 12 = 80. That size is reasonable, because a great many 0.12s fit inside 9.6.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el último paso el dividendo se movió solo 1 lugar mientras que el divisor se movió 2, así que los dos números ya no coinciden. Agregar un cero de relleno permite que 9.6 se mueva los dos lugares hasta 960, y el problema real es 960 ÷ 12 = 80. Ese tamaño tiene sentido, porque muchísimos 0.12 caben dentro de 9.6.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Ambos números deben moverse la MISMA cantidad de lugares — 2, no 1. A 9.6 se le acaban los dígitos después de un lugar, así que anexas un cero de relleno para mover el segundo lugar: 9.6 → 96 → 960. El problema real es 960 ÷ 12 = 80, así que 9.6 ÷ 0.12 = 80. Estima para confirmar: 0.12 es pequeñísimo, así que caben muchos en 9.6 — el cociente debe ser grande, no 8. Comprueba: 80 × 0.12 = 9.6. ✓

onLevel.title: Find Derek's Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: Derek only multiplied by 10, but the divisor 0.45 has two decimal places. He should multiply both numbers by 100: 720 ÷ 45 = 16. He got the right answer by luck this time, but his method is unreliable because the divisor is still a decimal (4.5).
hints: How many decimal places does 0.45 have? Did Derek multiply by enough to make it a whole number?
0.45 has two decimal places, so multiply both by 100, not 10. 0.45 × 100 = 45 and 7.2 × 100 = 720.
onLevel.explanation: In the step where Derek multiplied by 10, the divisor only became 4.5 — still a decimal, so the setup was never finished. Because 0.45 has two decimal places, both numbers need ×100, giving 720 ÷ 45 = 16. The quotient does not change, but leaving a decimal divisor makes the long division far harder than it needs to be.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el paso donde Derek multiplicó por 10, el divisor solo llegó a 4.5, que sigue siendo un decimal, así que el planteamiento nunca se terminó. Como 0.45 tiene dos lugares decimales, los dos números necesitan ×100, lo que da 720 ÷ 45 = 16. El cociente no cambia, pero dejar un divisor decimal vuelve la división mucho más difícil de lo necesario.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Derek solo multiplicó por 10, pero el divisor 0.45 tiene dos lugares decimales. Debía multiplicar ambos números por 100: 720 ÷ 45 = 16. Esta vez obtuvo la respuesta correcta por suerte, pero su método no es confiable porque el divisor sigue siendo un decimal (4.5).

onLevel.prompt: A gas station sells fuel at $3.45 per gallon. A customer pays $27.60 total. How many gallons did the customer buy? Set up the decimal division, show how to convert it to whole-number division, and solve.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: The equation is $27.60 ÷ $3.45 = ___. I multiply both by ___ to get ___ ÷ ___ = ___ gallons.
hints: Total money ÷ price per gallon = gallons, so set up 27.60 ÷ 3.45 — and notice the divisor has TWO decimal places.
Multiply both numbers by 100 so the divisor becomes a whole number, then divide the two new whole numbers.
27.60 × 100 = 2,760 and 3.45 × 100 = 345. Now ask how many 345s fit into 2,760 — note that 345 × 10 = 3,450 is already too big.
onLevel.explanation: Total cost divided by price per gallon gives the number of gallons, so the setup is 27.60 ÷ 3.45. The divisor has two decimal places, so multiplying both numbers by 100 gives 2,760 ÷ 345 = 8 gallons, and 8 × $3.45 = $27.60 confirms it.
onLevel.explanationEs: El costo total dividido entre el precio por galón da la cantidad de galones, así que el planteamiento es 27.60 ÷ 3.45. El divisor tiene dos lugares decimales, así que multiplicar los dos números por 100 da 2,760 ÷ 345 = 8 galones, y 8 × $3.45 = $27.60 lo confirma.
onLevel.promptEs: Una gasolinera vende combustible a $3.45 por galón. Un cliente paga $27.60 en total. ¿Cuántos galones compró? Plantea la división de decimales, muestra cómo convertirla en una división de números enteros y resuelve.
hintsEs: Dinero total ÷ precio por galón = galones, así que plantea 27.60 ÷ 3.45, y fíjate que el divisor tiene DOS decimales.
Multiplica ambos números por 100 para que el divisor sea entero y luego divide los dos números nuevos.
27.60 × 100 = 2,760 y 3.45 × 100 = 345. Ahora pregunta cuántos 345 caben en 2,760; nota que 345 × 10 = 3,450 ya es demasiado.

choiceFeedback: Check: 0.8 × 0.6 is only 0.48, so 0.8 is ten times too small. Multiply both numbers by 10 first — then it's just 48 ÷ 6 with no extra decimal shift.
Ten times too large — that happens when only 4.8 gets multiplied by 10. Scale both numbers the same way.
That looks like a subtraction (4.8 − 0.6) rather than a division. Reread the operation sign.
hints: Dividing by a decimal is easiest when the divisor is a whole number. Ask yourself what 0.6 needs to become.
Multiply the divisor and the dividend by the same power of 10. Here, multiplying by 10 does the job.
Multiplying both by 10 turns the problem into 48 ÷ 6. Carry out that division to finish.
hintsEs: Dividir entre un decimal es más fácil cuando el divisor es un número entero. Pregúntate en qué debe convertirse 0.6.
Multiplica el divisor y el dividendo por la misma potencia de 10. Aquí, multiplicar por 10 es suficiente.
Multiplicar ambos por 10 convierte el problema en 48 ÷ 6. Realiza esa división para terminar.

choiceFeedback: 1.05 × 0.9 is only 0.945 — the decimal moved one spot too far left. Shift both numbers by the same amount so the problem becomes 94.5 ÷ 9.
The digits are right, but the value is 10 times too large. Recheck where the decimal point lands in the quotient.
That is nearly 9.45 itself, which would mean dividing by about 1. Since 0.9 is less than 1, the quotient has to be noticeably larger than 9.45.
hints: The divisor 0.9 is less than 1, so the quotient will be larger than 9.45. That is your size check.
Multiply the divisor and the dividend by the same power of 10 so the divisor becomes a whole number.
Multiplying both by 10 gives 94.5 ÷ 9. Divide, keeping the decimal point lined up.
hintsEs: El divisor 0.9 es menor que 1, así que el cociente será mayor que 9.45. Esa es tu comprobación de tamaño.
Multiplica el divisor y el dividendo por la misma potencia de 10 para que el divisor sea un número entero.
Multiplicar ambos por 10 da 94.5 ÷ 9. Divide manteniendo alineado el punto decimal.

extending.stem: A ribbon is 7.2 meters long and is cut into 0.8-meter pieces. How many pieces are there?
choiceFeedback: 8 pieces would use only 8 × 0.8 = 6.4 meters, leaving ribbon left over. Multiply both numbers by 10 and divide 72 by 8 to count every piece.
Careful — the 7 comes from 7.2, not from dividing. Set up 72 ÷ 8 and work it out.
A little too high. Ten pieces of 0.8 meters would need 8 meters of ribbon, and you only have 7.2.
extending.stemEs: Un listón mide 7.2 metros de largo y se corta en pedazos de 0.8 metros. ¿Cuántos pedazos hay?
hints: Cutting a length into equal pieces is a division: total length ÷ length of one piece.
Make the divisor a whole number by multiplying both 7.2 and 0.8 by 10.
That turns the problem into 72 ÷ 8. Count how many 8s fit into 72.
hintsEs: Cortar una longitud en pedazos iguales es una división: longitud total ÷ longitud de un pedazo.
Convierte el divisor en número entero multiplicando 7.2 y 0.8 por 10.
Eso convierte el problema en 72 ÷ 8. Cuenta cuántos 8 caben en 72.

extending.explanation: Dividing by 0.25 is like multiplying by 4: 15 × 4 = 60.
choiceFeedback: Move both decimals two places so the divisor is whole: 1500 ÷ 25 = 60. Dividing by a number smaller than 1 makes the result LARGER, not smaller.
That is 15 ÷ 10. Dividing by 0.25 is not the same as sliding the decimal point one place.
Dividing by a number less than 1 makes the result larger, not smaller. 0.6 is far below 15.
extending.explanationEs: Dividir entre 0.25 es lo mismo que multiplicar por 4: 15 × 4 = 60.
hints: Think about how many quarters fit inside one whole — 0.25 is one quarter.
If four 0.25s fit in every 1, then dividing by 0.25 does the same job as multiplying by 4.
So the problem becomes 15 × 4. Work that product out.
hintsEs: Piensa cuántos cuartos caben en un entero: 0.25 es un cuarto.
Si cuatro veces 0.25 caben en cada 1, entonces dividir entre 0.25 hace lo mismo que multiplicar por 4.
Así el problema se convierte en 15 × 4. Calcula ese producto.

extending.stem: Table 1 splits a $15.00 lunch bill equally among 4 friends. How much does each friend pay?
choiceFeedback: $3.05 × 4 = $12.20, which doesn't cover the $15.00 bill. When 15 ÷ 4 leaves a remainder, keep dividing into the tenths and hundredths — don't skip a decimal place.
That is more than a quarter of $15.00. Four payments of $5.30 would come to over $21.
This is larger than the whole bill, so it cannot be one person's share. Divide by 4 instead of multiplying.
extending.stemEs: La mesa 1 divide en partes iguales una cuenta de almuerzo de $15.00 entre 4 amigos. ¿Cuánto paga cada amigo?
hints: Splitting a bill equally means dividing the total by the number of people.
Set up 15.00 ÷ 4. The divisor is already a whole number, so no scaling is needed.
4 goes into 15 three times with 3 left over. Bring down the decimal digits and keep dividing.
hintsEs: Dividir una cuenta en partes iguales significa dividir el total entre el número de personas.
Plantea 15.00 ÷ 4. El divisor ya es un número entero, así que no hace falta escalar.
El 4 cabe tres veces en 15 y sobran 3. Baja las cifras decimales y sigue dividiendo.

extending.stem: A recipe uses 9.6 cups of flour to make 3 equal batches of muffins. How many cups of flour go in each batch?
choiceFeedback: 2.3 × 3 = 6.9 cups, which is less than the 9.6 cups used. Divide the 9 by 3, then the 6 tenths by 3, and check each digit.
The digits are right, but 32 cups is far more than you started with. Check where the decimal point belongs in the quotient.
That looks like 9.6 - 3. The word 'each' here signals division, not subtraction.
extending.stemEs: Una receta usa 9.6 tazas de harina para hacer 3 tandas iguales de panecillos. ¿Cuántas tazas de harina lleva cada tanda?
hints: Equal batches means the flour is shared evenly, so this is a division.
Divide the total flour by the number of batches: 9.6 ÷ 3.
3 goes into 9 three times; then bring down the .6 and keep going.
hintsEs: Tandas iguales significa que la harina se reparte por igual, así que esto es una división.
Divide la harina total entre el número de tandas: 9.6 ÷ 3.
El 3 cabe tres veces en 9; después baja el .6 y continúa.

extending.stem: The arcade corner has 8.1 meters of token ribbon, cut into 0.9-meter prize strips. How many strips can the cafe make?
choiceFeedback: 0.9 is less than one strip — dividing 8.1 by 0.9 must give MORE strips, not less than one. Multiply both numbers by 10 and divide 81 by 9.
Ten times too many — that happens when only 8.1 is multiplied by 10. Scale both numbers together.
8.1 is the total length in meters, not the number of strips. You still need to divide it by 0.9.
extending.stemEs: El rincón de videojuegos tiene 8.1 metros de listón de fichas, que se corta en tiras de premio de 0.9 metros. ¿Cuántas tiras puede hacer el café?
hints: How many 0.9-meter pieces fit inside 8.1 meters? That question is a division.
Multiply both 8.1 and 0.9 by 10 so the divisor becomes a whole number.
The problem becomes 81 ÷ 9. Finish the division from there.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántos pedazos de 0.9 metros caben en 8.1 metros? Esa pregunta es una división.
Multiplica 8.1 y 0.9 por 10 para que el divisor sea un número entero.
El problema se convierte en 81 ÷ 9. Termina la división desde ahí.

extending.title: Level 2 Extension — The Misplaced Decimal at the Register

workedExample.label: Order
workedExample.work: A $13.50 catering tray is split into 0.45-pound scoops. How many scoops?
workedExample.workEs: Una bandeja de catering de $13.50 se reparte en porciones de 0.45 libras. ¿Cuántas porciones salen?

workedExample.label: Divide and place the decimal
workedExample.labelEs: Divide y coloca el punto decimal

extending.correctWork: Moving both points 2 places gives 1350 ÷ 45, which equals 30, not 3.0 — the decimal point was placed one spot too far left. So 13.50 ÷ 0.45 = 30 scoops. Check: 30 × 0.45 = 13.50. ✓
hints: After you rewrite it as 1350 ÷ 45, estimate first: about how many 45s fit in 1350? That is much more than 3.
1350 ÷ 45 = 30. The cashier slid the decimal one place too far left, turning 30 into 3.0.
extending.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: el punto decimal mal colocado en la caja
extending.explanation: The rewrite to 1350 ÷ 45 was done correctly, but the final step placed the decimal point one spot too far left. Since 45 × 30 = 1,350, the answer is 30 scoops, not 3.0, and 30 × 0.45 = 13.50 confirms it.
extending.explanationEs: La reescritura a 1350 ÷ 45 se hizo correctamente, pero el paso final colocó el punto decimal un lugar demasiado a la izquierda. Como 45 × 30 = 1,350, la respuesta es 30 porciones, no 3.0, y 30 × 0.45 = 13.50 lo confirma.
extending.correctWorkEs: Mover ambos puntos 2 lugares da 1350 ÷ 45, que es igual a 30, no 3.0 — el punto decimal quedó un lugar demasiado a la izquierda. Así que 13.50 ÷ 0.45 = 30 porciones. Comprueba: 30 × 0.45 = 13.50. ✓

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Decimals is moving the decimal point in the divisor but forgetting to move it the same number of places in the dividend. For example, in 6.4 ÷ 0.8 a student changes 0.8 to 8 but leaves the dividend as 6.4, then divides 6.4 ÷ 8 = 0.8 instead of moving both points to get 64 ÷ 8 = 8. A second version of this mistake happens when the divisor has two decimal places, like 0.12: students move both points only 1 place instead of 2, turning 9.6 ÷ 0.12 into 96 ÷ 1.2 instead of the correct 960 ÷ 12. Count the divisor's decimal places first, then move BOTH points that same number of places.

optionalActivity.name: Decimal Cafe Portion Lab
optionalActivity.intro: Challenge — prove it: Welcome to the Decimal Cafe — divide money, recipes, and game tokens into equal portions to keep every table served. Convince a skeptic your answer is right.

connect.scenario: A ribbon is 16.8 feet long. You need to cut it into pieces that are each 2.4 feet long for a craft project.
connect.promptQuestion: How does decimal division help you figure out how many pieces you can cut?

check.explanation: Multiply both numbers by 10 to clear the decimal: 168 ÷ 24 = 7. Check: 2.4 × 7 = 16.8.

choices: Multiplying both numbers by 10 keeps the quotient the same
Because decimals are not allowed in division
Because you always drop the decimal point
check.explanation: Division compares two amounts. Scaling both by the same factor of 10 does not change how many times one fits into the other.

check.stem: If each piece were 2.8 feet instead, how many whole pieces could you cut?
check.explanation: 16.8 ÷ 2.8 = 6. Longer pieces means fewer of them fit.

connect.modelAnswer: 16.8 ÷ 2.4 = 7 pieces. Multiply both numbers by 10 to get 168 ÷ 24 = 7, then check by multiplying back: 2.4 × 7 = 16.8.
